title: Redirected descendants can continue after the owned run ends

significance.impact: Work in the provider's process group can continue after cancellation, timeout, or normal leader exit.
significance.exposure: Every run_bounded consumer whose provider leaves same-group descendants that redirect all standard streams; TERM-resistant children expose the termination path.
significance.detectability: The leader's exit and closed pipes appear complete while the descendant remains active.
significance.systemic_implication: The shared process boundary must release the entire owned group independently of direct-child wait and pipe-drain state.
significance.recovery: The local process boundary is repairable. A returned cancellation cannot roll back already performed actions; no historical provider-side effect was established by these fixtures.
significance.rationale: A shared lifecycle invariant fails under specific descendant or observation conditions. The observed scope warrants a transport-wide repair and regressions, not a claim of arbitrary process containment.

confidence.basis: Independent source inspection followed by real-process pre-fix reproduction at the intended liveness assertions.

evidence.observation: All cancel, timeout, and leader_exit regressions reached a ready TERM-resistant descendant; after run_bounded returned, a test trigger caused the surviving descendant to write a marker.
139 affected tests passed after the ownership/idempotence repair; these are source tests, not installed native permission qualification.

claim.failure_mode: Termination escalates only when the direct leader times out; normal leader exit with redirected descendants never reaches pipe-triggered cleanup.
claim.downstream_consequence: Callers may report the run ended while owned work still performs local or provider actions.

counterevidence.observation: The existing retained-output-pipe and parent-death checks exercise different paths and passed; they did not reject these five reproduced failures.

proof_limits: Same-group, same-user local processes only; detached sessions and hostile privilege changes are not contained by a process group.
No native provider action, installed-runtime qualification, or recovery/cancellation acknowledgement has been proven.

containment: Move ownership outside observation/setup, unconditionally escalate the group, and make stop idempotent so completed cleanup is not signaled twice.

remediation.description: Move ownership outside observation/setup, unconditionally escalate the group, and make stop idempotent so completed cleanup is not signaled twice.
Independently review the repaired lifecycle and exercise its installed approval/recovery consumers before claiming E1 closure.

required: Preserve all five pre-fix assertion rejections as permanent real-process regressions.
An independent reviewer must assess the repaired source and outstanding lifecycle conditions.
